description: Knowledge Acquisition system — a multi-provider search and knowledge flywheel that acquires external knowledge (web search, vulnerability intelligence, API documentation, UI Bridge snapshots), summarizes it, embeds it, and stores it in task_knowledge for future retrieval. Tiered routing: Tier 0 (local cache via hybrid_search) → Tier 1 (UI Bridge) → Tier 2 (DuckDuckGo → Tavily → Perplexity) → Tier 3 (ingest into task_knowledge). Exposed via 9 HTTP API endpoints at /knowledge/* and 6 registered MCP tools. Supports both SQLite (CheckpointDb) and PostgreSQL (PgDb) backends.

groups.name: Provider Availability and Status
groups.description: The /knowledge/providers endpoint reports which search providers are available and whether they require API keys. Free providers (DuckDuckGo, Sploitus, OSV.dev) are always available. Paid providers (Tavily, Perplexity) require API keys via environment variables. UI Bridge availability is checked dynamically at search time. This information helps users understand what search capabilities are active and what configuration is needed to unlock additional providers.

assertions.description: The provider list displays all 6 providers: duckduckgo, tavily, ui_bridge, sploitus, osv_dev, perplexity. Each shows its name, availability status (boolean), and whether it requires an API key.
DuckDuckGo, Sploitus, and OSV.dev must always show available=true regardless of configuration. These providers require no API keys and are the baseline capability of the system.

Tavily shows requires_api_key=true and is available only when TAVILY_API_KEY environment variable is set. Perplexity shows requires_api_key=true and is available only when PERPLEXITY_API_KEY is set. If keys are not configured, these providers report available=false but searches still work using free providers.

groups.name: Tiered Search Routing and Escalation
groups.description: The knowledge acquisition coordinator implements a 4-tier escalation strategy. Tier 0 checks local task_knowledge via hybrid_search (cosine similarity ≥0.5). If matches found, returns immediately (cache hit). Tier 1 queries UI Bridge if a connected app is available. Tier 2 escalates through web search providers: DuckDuckGo first (free, fast), then Tavily if <2 results and API key available, then Perplexity as last resort if still empty. Tier 3 stores results via the ingestor. This architecture ensures the system learns from every search — subsequent identical queries are served from local cache.

assertions.description: When local task_knowledge contains entries with cosine similarity ≥0.5 to the query, the search returns immediately with provider='local_knowledge' results. No external API calls are made. The stats endpoint should show cache_hits incrementing for these queries.

When DuckDuckGo returns fewer than 2 results and Tavily is available, the system automatically escalates to Tavily. If both DDG and Tavily return empty and Perplexity is available, it escalates to Perplexity. Each escalation step is visible in the provider_used array of the response. The stats endpoint shows query counts increasing on the escalated providers.

After a successful web search, results are automatically summarized (if >3000 chars), embedded via MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-dim), deduplicated (cosine >0.85 = skip), and stored in task_knowledge with category='external_knowledge' and agent_type='system'. The stats endpoint shows results_ingested and dedup_skipped incrementing. Subsequent searches for the same topic should hit Tier 0 cache.

Each search session is capped at 5 actions, 80KB total content, 50KB per result, and 30s timeout per provider call. When the budget is exhausted, remaining tiers are skipped gracefully. Over-large results are truncated at safe UTF-8 boundaries before storage.

groups.name: Web Search Results (DuckDuckGo / Tavily)
groups.description: The /knowledge/search-web endpoint performs general web search. DuckDuckGo results are parsed from HTML using cached regexes — titles, URLs (with DDG redirect URL decoding), and snippets are extracted. Tavily results include AI-synthesized answers with raw page content. Each result is formatted as markdown with title, snippet, and source URL. Results include provider identification so consumers know which source produced each result.

assertions.description: Each search result contains: provider (string identifier), query (original search text), title (result heading), content (markdown-formatted body), url (source link, optional), relevance_score (0-1 float, optional), and metadata object with domain classification.

DuckDuckGo result URLs are correctly decoded from DDG redirect format (//duckduckgo.com/l/?uddg=...) to actual target URLs. Multi-byte UTF-8 percent-encoded characters in URLs are correctly decoded (e.g., %C3%A9 → é). Protocol-relative URLs (//) are prefixed with https:.

When Tavily is available and used, the first result may be an AI-synthesized answer (title starts with 'AI Answer:'). This provides a direct answer to the query synthesized from multiple web sources, followed by individual source results with relevance scores. Raw content from pages is capped at 50KB per result.
assertions.precondition: Tavily API key is configured and DuckDuckGo returned <2 results

groups.name: Error Research Compound Search
groups.description: The /knowledge/research-error endpoint performs compound search optimized for error resolution. It builds a search query from the error message, optional framework context, and the first meaningful line from a stack trace (skipping 'at ' frames and node_modules). Uses KnowledgeDomain::ErrorResolution which triggers Tier 0 cache lookup and Tier 3 storage via the knowledge flywheel. This is the highest-value integration point — the fix agent calls it automatically when encountering unfamiliar errors.

assertions.description: The search query is constructed from: (1) framework prefix if provided (e.g., 'React'), (2) the error message, (3) first meaningful stack trace line (non-empty, not starting with 'at ', not containing 'node_modules'). This compound query produces more relevant results than the raw error message alone.

The orchestration loop's fix agent automatically calls knowledge acquisition when building fix prompts. Error descriptions from reflection fixes are joined, truncated at a safe UTF-8 boundary (200 chars), and searched with a 15-second timeout. Up to 3 results are appended to the fix prompt as 'External Research Context' sections, each showing title, provider, and content (capped at 1500 chars).
assertions.precondition: A workflow is running and the fix agent phase is active

groups.name: Vulnerability Intelligence (Sploitus / OSV.dev)
groups.description: The /knowledge/search-vulnerabilities endpoint queries Sploitus for exploit data by software name, version, or CVE ID. Results include exploit source code (capped at 50KB), CVSS scores with severity classification (Critical ≥9.0, High ≥7.0, Medium ≥4.0, Low), publication dates, and links to original sources. The /knowledge/audit-dependencies and /knowledge/audit-manifest endpoints query OSV.dev for structured vulnerability data by package ecosystem and version. Supported ecosystems: npm, PyPI, crates.io, Go, Maven, NuGet.

assertions.description: Vulnerability results display CVSS scores with severity labels: CRITICAL (≥9.0), HIGH (≥7.0), MEDIUM (≥4.0), LOW (<4.0). CVE IDs are extracted from result titles and stored in metadata. Exploit availability is indicated per result.

The dependency audit accepts a list of packages (name, ecosystem, version) and batch-queries OSV.dev. Up to 1000 packages per batch. Results are grouped by package name with per-package vulnerability lists. Each vulnerability includes CVE ID, summary, details, CVSS score, affected version ranges, and fixed version (when available). Unrecognized ecosystems are reported in skipped_ecosystems rather than silently dropped.

The /knowledge/audit-manifest endpoint parses manifest files directly: package.json (npm dependencies + devDependencies, skips workspace:* and * versions), Cargo.toml (dependencies + dev-dependencies + build-dependencies, rejects workspace-root Cargo.toml with descriptive error), pyproject.toml (PEP 621 [project.dependencies] and Poetry [tool.poetry.dependencies], strips ^/~/>=  prefixes, skips python entry). Semver prefixes are stripped to extract clean version numbers for OSV lookup.

When a Security-category finding is inserted during a Claude session, an async task spawns that extracts CVE IDs from the finding description, queries Sploitus for exploit data, and stores the enrichment (CVE IDs, max CVSS score, exploit count, remediation guidance, references) as a task_knowledge entry with category='vulnerability_enrichment'. This enrichment is fire-and-forget — it does not block finding insertion.
assertions.precondition: A Security-category finding has been detected during workflow execution

groups.name: Observability and Statistics
groups.description: The /knowledge/stats endpoint returns a point-in-time snapshot of all knowledge acquisition metrics accumulated since process start. This includes per-provider query counts, success/failure/timeout rates, total searches, cache hit rate (Tier 0 hits / total searches), ingestion counts, dedup skip counts, and prompt injection detection counts. All counters use atomic operations for thread safety. The stats are served from the global singleton coordinator instance, so they reflect all search activity across the process.

assertions.description: The stats snapshot contains per-provider metrics for all 7 providers (local_knowledge, ui_bridge, duckduckgo, tavily, perplexity, sploitus, osv). Each provider shows: queries (total attempts), successes, failures, timeouts, results_returned (cumulative), bytes_fetched (cumulative), and success_rate (successes/queries, 0.0 if no queries).

The cache_hit_rate field shows what fraction of total searches were served from local task_knowledge (Tier 0) without any external API calls. A high cache hit rate indicates the knowledge flywheel is working — previous searches are being reused. A rate of 0.0 with nonzero total_searches means no queries have been served from cache yet.

The injection_detections counter tracks how many ingested results were flagged by the prompt injection scanner. Flagged content is not dropped — it is stored with an [INJECTION_WARNING] prefix. The scanner detects known injection phrases ('ignore previous instructions', 'system prompt:', etc.), credential exfiltration patterns, and invisible Unicode characters (zero-width spaces, RTL overrides).

groups.name: Dual-Database Backend (SQLite + PostgreSQL)
groups.description: The knowledge acquisition system supports both SQLite (CheckpointDb) and PostgreSQL (PgDb) backends. When DATABASE_URL is set, SearchContext attempts a PG connection at creation time. All operations (Tier 0 hybrid search, Tier 3 insert/embed/dedup) prefer PG when available and fall back to SQLite. The PG schema includes task_knowledge table with content_embedding BYTEA column. Hybrid search uses the same rank_results algorithm on both backends: fetch recent candidates with embeddings, compute cosine similarity in-memory (MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim), rank by 30% SQL position + 70% vector similarity.

assertions.description: When PostgreSQL is unavailable (no DATABASE_URL, connection failure), the system operates entirely on SQLite with no user-visible degradation. All 9 API endpoints continue to function. The /knowledge/providers endpoint shows the same available providers regardless of which database backend is active.

Embeddings are stored as BYTEA in PostgreSQL (f32 little-endian bytes, 1536 bytes for 384 dimensions). The same vector_to_blob/blob_to_vector conversion functions are used for both SQLite BLOB and PG BYTEA, ensuring embedding data is portable between backends.

PostgreSQL timestamps are formatted as ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MI:SSZ) via to_char() for consistency with SQLite datetime strings. This ensures created_at values are parseable by chrono::DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339 regardless of which backend produced them.

groups.name: MCP Tool Registrations for AI Agents
groups.description: Six knowledge acquisition tools are registered in the AgentToolRegistry for autonomous use by Claude sessions during workflows. Each tool has a descriptive LLM-friendly description that helps the AI decide which tool to use: search_web (quick facts), research_error (error debugging with escalation), search_vulnerabilities (exploit/CVE lookup), audit_dependencies (batch OSV check), lookup_api_docs (deep documentation search), audit_manifest (parse manifest + audit). Tools are tagged with 'knowledge' plus role-specific tags (search, debugging, security, documentation).

assertions.description: The AgentToolRegistry contains exactly 6 knowledge acquisition tools: search_web, research_error, search_vulnerabilities, audit_dependencies, lookup_api_docs, audit_manifest. Each is assigned to the appropriate agent role (researcher or security_analyst).

Each tool description includes guidance on when to use vs not use it. search_web says 'NOT for deep research'. lookup_api_docs says 'slower than search_web — use only when quick search is insufficient'. search_vulnerabilities specifies 'by software name, version, or CVE ID'. This helps AI agents select the right tool without trial and error.

groups.name: Query Tool Web Integration
groups.description: The existing /query endpoint's QueryType enum includes a 'web' variant that delegates to the knowledge acquisition coordinator. This allows Claude sessions to search the web through the same query_runner_data interface used for SQL, vector, and hybrid database queries. The web variant accepts search_text (required), limit, and an optional filters.domain ('vulnerability', 'error', 'api', or defaults to 'general') to classify the search. Results are returned in the standard QueryRunnerDataResponse format with provider, title, content, url, and relevance_score fields.

assertions.description: Sending query_type='web' with search_text to the /query endpoint performs a knowledge acquisition search with the full flywheel (Tier 0 cache check, Tier 2 web search, Tier 3 storage). Results are formatted as JSON values in the standard query response format. The metadata shows query_type='web' and embedding_used=false.

groups.name: Prompt Injection Detection on Ingested Content
groups.description: All content ingested from external sources passes through a prompt injection scanner before storage. The scanner detects: injection phrases (21 patterns including 'ignore previous instructions', 'system prompt:', 'jailbreak', 'developer mode'), credential exfiltration attempts (6 patterns like 'exfiltrate', 'send api key to'), and invisible Unicode characters (16 types including zero-width spaces, RTL overrides, word joiners). Flagged content is NOT dropped — it is prefixed with [INJECTION_WARNING: N suspicious patterns detected: ...] for transparency. This allows downstream consumers to make informed decisions while preserving the content for analysis.

assertions.description: When prompt injection is detected in ingested content, the content is stored with an [INJECTION_WARNING] prefix listing matched patterns. The original content is preserved below the warning. This follows the principle of transparency over silent removal — the content may contain legitimate technical documentation about prompt injection that happens to match patterns.
assertions.precondition: External content containing injection patterns has been ingested

assertions.description: The scanner detects invisible Unicode characters that could be used to hide instructions: zero-width space (U+200B), zero-width joiner (U+200D), right-to-left override (U+202E), and 13 other invisibles. These are counted and reported in the warning prefix but not stripped from the content.
assertions.precondition: Content with invisible Unicode characters has been ingested

groups.name: HTTP API Endpoints
groups.description: Nine HTTP endpoints exposed under /knowledge/*: GET /knowledge/providers (list provider availability), GET /knowledge/stats (observability metrics), POST /knowledge/search-web (general web search), POST /knowledge/research-error (error research with escalation), POST /knowledge/fetch-page (UI Bridge snapshot), POST /knowledge/lookup-api-docs (deep API docs search), POST /knowledge/search-vulnerabilities (exploit/CVE search), POST /knowledge/audit-dependencies (batch package audit), POST /knowledge/audit-manifest (parse manifest + audit). All POST endpoints return {success, data: {results, provider_used}} wrapped in ApiResponse.

assertions.description: All knowledge API endpoints return the standard ApiResponse format: {success: boolean, data?: T, error?: string}. Search endpoints return data with {results: KnowledgeResult[], provider_used: string[]}. Audit endpoints return {packages: [{package_name, vulns}], total_vulns, skipped_ecosystems?}. Error responses include descriptive error messages.

If all external providers fail (network down, rate limited, timeouts), search endpoints return success=true with an empty results array — never success=false. Provider failures are logged but never propagated as errors to the caller. The system degrades gracefully: fewer results, not broken responses.

groups.name: Singleton Coordinator Architecture
groups.description: The KnowledgeAcquisition coordinator is a global singleton (OnceLock<Arc<...>>), shared across all call sites in the process. This ensures: (1) the DuckDuckGo 2-second rate limiter is globally effective, (2) reqwest::Client connection pools are shared, (3) stats counters accumulate correctly across all API handlers and background tasks, (4) provider initialization (env var reads, health checks) happens once. The singleton is created on first access via KnowledgeAcquisition::new().

assertions.description: The DuckDuckGo provider enforces a 2-second minimum delay between requests using a shared Arc<Mutex<Instant>>. Because all callers share the singleton, concurrent searches queue behind the rate limiter. This prevents DuckDuckGo from blocking the runner's IP. The rate limiter is per-process, not per-request.

Because all code paths share the singleton, the /knowledge/stats endpoint reflects cumulative activity from: API route handlers, query_tool Web variant, fix agent knowledge enrichment, and security finding enrichment tasks. The uptime_secs field shows seconds since the singleton was created (typically process start).
